sections.h2: Who sets and collects property tax in Luzerne County
sections.html:
Luzerne County's Assessment Office sets a value on every parcel. Your municipality and school district each apply a millage rate to that value, and the combined amounts make up the bill you receive.

With 76 municipalities and a dozen school districts in the county, the list of districts is long: Wilkes-Barre Area, Hazleton Area, Wyoming Valley West, Pittston Area, Dallas, Crestwood, Greater Nanticoke Area, Hanover Area, Lake-Lehman, Northwest Area, Wyoming Area and Berwick Area. So two houses assessed at the same figure can still have different yearly bills. Look at the taxing bodies printed on your bill before you price against a house in the next town.

You can reach the Assessor's Office at 570-825-1540 or visit the Courthouse Annex, 153 North River Street, Wilkes-Barre. It is open weekdays from 9:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The Hazleton branch is open Tuesdays and Thursdays, 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. Appeals board mail goes to 200 North River Street, Wilkes-Barre, PA 18711.

Send the appeal form to the Board of Assessment Appeals with a check to the County of Luzerne. The amount comes from the county's appeal filing fee schedule. A written notice with the hearing date, time and place follows. There are separate forms for single-family homes, multi-family residential property and vacant land.

The single-family form asks for what a board wants to see:

  • The tax map identification number, with map, block and lot.
  • The purchase date and price, plus a copy of the current deed.
  • The assessment you are appealing, split into land and improvements, and what you think the property is worth.
  • Annual rent, if the property is rented.
  • Your reasons for the appeal, signed under penalty for false statements.

By filing you agree to a hearing and a decision after October 31, and one, two or three board members may hear the case. The board can raise an assessment as well as lower it, so a weak appeal can backfire. Call the Assessment Office for this year's filing deadline before you start. Gather your deed and your purchase paperwork first, since the form asks for both, and keep a copy of everything you file. Notice of the hearing arrives by mail, so make sure the office has your current address.

Back taxes can be paid at the courthouse, though the Assessment Office does not issue tax bills. Visit the Tax Claim Bureau first, because it prepares the statement showing what you owe. Only cash and checks are accepted for these payments, not credit cards.

Taxes left unpaid can lead to a tax sale. The county's ordinance names four types: upset, private, judicial free and clear, and repository. The Tax Claim Bureau or its agent conducts each under the Pennsylvania Real Estate Tax Sale Law (72 P.S. 5860.101 and following). A $100.00 fee has applied to every buyer at a tax sale since March 1, 2026, and the sheriff charges the same at mortgage foreclosure sales. Proceeds feed a county Demolition and Rehabilitation Fund aimed at blighted buildings. Nonprofits, land banks and government bodies are exempt.

County Council adopted Ordinance 2026-08 on May 26, 2026 by an 11 to 0 vote. The ordinance puts in place the $15.00 charge that Act 152 of 2016 permits on each deed and mortgage recorded here. Revenue is held in its own Luzerne County Demolition Fund and may be spent only on tearing down blighted property. A plan is due to the state Department of Community and Economic Development within 90 days, with a report every year afterward.

The ordinance treats a property as blighted when it meets at least three of the criteria in section 5(d)(5) of the state's Abandoned and Blighted Property Conservatorship Act. It took effect 15 days after adoption, and the Recorder began collecting the amount on July 1, 2026. On your settlement statement it shows up as a separate charge.

sections.h2: What to have ready before you list
sections.html:
Pull together the paperwork that touches the county before you list. Your last tax bill shows your municipality, your school district and the parcel identification. The deed and the purchase date and price are what the appeal form asks for, so keep them in one folder. If you plan to challenge the assessment, the filing has to go in before you sell, since the hearing happens on the county calendar and not on your closing date.

For the closing itself, expect the title company to ask the Tax Claim Bureau and the municipality for current balances, so it is faster if you already know whether anything is open.

The county has 135,055 households and 151,965 housing units. Permits issued in 2025 numbered 295, and 89.3 percent of residents were in the same house a year earlier. The estimated population was 332,126 in July 2025, up 2.0 percent from the 2020 base.

sections.h2: Property tax and transfer costs at closing
sections.html:
Three county charges can appear at a Luzerne County closing, separate from the tax bill.

  • Recording: the Recorder of Deeds schedule effective November 17, 2025 sets $72.75 for a deed or mortgage, and an extra $15.00 has applied to deeds and mortgages since July 1, 2026 for the county demolition fund.
  • PIN certification: the Assessor's Office certifies the parcel number on every deed and bills its own fee. Call 570-825-1525 for the amount.
  • Transfer tax: the county's schedule lists a 2 percent total in most municipalities, 3.5 percent in Wilkes-Barre and Pittston, and 2.5 percent in Kingston Borough. Hazleton's total is 2 percent.

Your purchase agreement says who pays the transfer tax. Both sides are liable to the state, so read that clause before accepting an offer.

The current year's real estate tax is prorated between you and the buyer. Have the closing agent explain the split, and check that the bill used matches your municipality and school district. A mix-up there changes your payout.

Owe back taxes and want to sell? Request a payoff statement from the Tax Claim Bureau and hand it to the title company, which lists each open year and pays it at settlement. Paying the balance before a tax sale date keeps the county from forcing a sale of the house. The balance comes out of your sale proceeds, and you receive what is left.

One more call is worth making: ask your municipal office about any sewer, garbage or permit items tied to your address. Those are billed separately from the county tax.

faqs.q: Who do I call to dispute my Luzerne County assessment?
faqs.a: Call the Assessor's Office at 570-825-1540 or file the appeal form with the Board of Assessment Appeals. Include the filing fee check made out to the County of Luzerne.

faqs.q: Where do I pay delinquent Luzerne County property taxes?
faqs.a: Stop at the Tax Claim Bureau for a statement, then pay at the courthouse. Cash and checks work, but cards do not.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax in Wilkes-Barre?
faqs.a: The Recorder of Deeds schedule lists a 3.5 percent total for Wilkes-Barre. Most other municipalities show 2 percent, and Kingston Borough shows 2.5 percent.

faqs.q: Does Luzerne County charge a fee at tax sales?
faqs.a: Yes. Buyers at tax sales and mortgage foreclosure sales pay a $100.00 fee, in place since March 1, 2026, and it goes to the demolition and rehabilitation fund.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Luzerne County?
faqs.a: The median value of owner-occupied homes is $174,100 for 2020 to 2024. Individual towns can differ widely from that figure.
